gym: Set the bar on a rack at chest height and unrack it with both feet under the bar.
Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders, wrists straight, elbows pointing down.
Leave enough space behind you to step back safely; use the rack safety pins.
Start with an empty bar until the movement feels steady.

home: At home, use a resistance band anchored at face height in a closed door instead of a cable.
gym: Set the cable pulley at face height and use the rope attachment.
Hold the rope with thumbs pointing back towards you.
Pull the rope ends apart beside your ears; keep your ribs down.
Choose a light weight: you should control the return without being pulled forward.

home: Only use a very stable, low step or bench that cannot slide; clear the floor around you.
Wear shoes with grip; skip this exercise on a slippery floor.
gym: Use a low plyo box or a fixed bench, never a stacked or wobbly surface.
Land with knees soft and in line with your toes.

home: Hold a wall, chair back or door frame lightly for balance.
Stand on the edge of a stair for a bigger range once the floor version feels easy.
gym: Use a step platform or the edge of a plate for more range, holding a rack for balance.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand to add load when bodyweight becomes easy.

home: Use a mat or carpet so your back is comfortable.
Move slowly; if your lower back lifts off the floor, reduce how far you reach.
gym: Use a gym mat in a quiet corner.
Hold a light plate or ball between hands for an extra challenge only when control is solid.

home: You need a stable, flat bench and dumbbells; do not use a sofa or soft surface.
Without a bench, do a floor press: lie on a mat and press from the floor.
gym: Sit on the end of a flat bench with the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and bring them to chest level.
Hold the dumbbells with palms facing your feet and wrists stacked over elbows.
Keep your feet flat and shoulder blades pulled gently back on the bench.
Lower to about chest level, elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your body.

home: Use dumbbells or filled water bottles; keep a slight bend in your knees.
Rest one hand on a chair seat if you want extra back support (one-arm version).
gym: Use a flat bench for support: one knee and one hand on the bench for the one-arm version.
Keep your neck in line with your back and look at the floor slightly ahead.
Pull the elbow towards your hip, not straight up to the shoulder.

home: Use dumbbells or filled water bottles; stand with your back against a wall to stop swinging.
gym: Choose dumbbells you can lift for all reps without leaning back.
Grip the handle in the middle, wrists straight, palms facing forward.
Keep elbows pinned beside your ribs; only your forearms move.

home: Clear a space about two steps long in front of you.
Hold a wall or chair for balance if needed.
gym: Hold dumbbells at your sides to add load once bodyweight lunges feel easy.
Use a clear lane away from equipment.

home: Use a mat on the floor; place your heels about a hand's length from your hips.
gym: Use a mat; for more challenge, rest a light dumbbell or plate across your hips and hold it with both hands.
Keep your chin slightly tucked and push through your heels.

home: Place hands flat on the floor, fingers spread, directly under or slightly wider than your shoulders.
Use a mat for comfort; start with knee or wall push-ups if needed.
gym: Use a bench or Smith bar for an incline push-up if full push-ups are too hard.
Hands slightly wider than shoulders, elbows angled about 45 degrees back, not flared out.

home: You need a clear hallway or room length; walk in a straight line.
gym: Use an open turf or studio area away from machines.
Hold dumbbells at your sides for extra load once balance is steady.

home: Place a chair behind you as a target and safety: lightly touch it and stand up.
Keep your weight across your whole foot, not only the toes.
gym: Hold a dumbbell at your chest (goblet squat) when bodyweight squats feel easy.
Use a box or bench behind you to control depth.
Set the bar in the rack at mid-chest height and the safety pins just below your lowest squat depth.
Grip the bar evenly, hands just outside your shoulders, wrists straight; rest it on your upper back, not your neck.
Step back only two or three small steps and set your feet shoulder-width apart.
Ask for a spotter or use safety pins; start with the empty bar.

home: Use a mat with a stable, non-slip surface.
Look at the floor between your hands and keep breathing.
gym: Use a mat. An elevated hand position on a stable bench is an easier variation.
Keep your hands under your shoulders; stop if your wrists hurt.

home: Use a mat; bend your knees for an easier version.
gym: Use a mat; keep your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Stack your hips; do not let the top hip roll backwards.

home: Use a mat; place a cushion under your knees if needed.
gym: Use a mat; imagine balancing a cup on your lower back to keep hips level.

home: Place hands on the wall at shoulder height and shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing up.
The further your feet are from the wall, the harder it becomes.
gym: Use a wall or a fixed rack upright; progress to an incline push-up on a bench.

home: Put a folded towel or mat under your knees.
Hands a little wider than shoulders, fingers forward.
gym: Use a mat; progress to an incline push-up on a bench, then to full push-ups.

home: Use light dumbbells or water bottles; sit on a sturdy chair with back support if standing is hard.
gym: Use a bench with the back upright for support.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward, wrists stacked over elbows.
Press up and slightly in; do not lock your elbows hard at the top.

home: Use very light dumbbells or water bottles; lighter is better here.
gym: Pick the lightest dumbbells first; heavy weights cause swinging.
Hold the dumbbells with palms facing your body and lead with your elbows.
A cable machine at hip height gives smoother resistance for one-arm raises.

home: Anchor the band in a closed door with a door anchor or around a sturdy post.
Check the band for cracks before every session.
gym: Use a cable row machine instead: sit tall, feet on the platform, knees slightly bent.
Hold the handle with palms facing each other and pull to your lower ribs.

home: Hold a broomstick along your back touching head, upper back and tailbone to learn a straight back.
gym: Use a dowel or PVC pipe along your back; later progress to a light kettlebell or dumbbell deadlift.

home: Use the bottom stair or a very stable, low step; hold the handrail.
gym: Use a fixed step platform or a low plyo box; hold dumbbells only when balance is solid.

home: Any clear space works; march on a carpet or mat to reduce impact.
gym: March in an open area or on a treadmill at slow walking speed holding the rails.

home: Use a wall or door frame for support.
gym: Use a wall or a rack upright for support.

home: Sit or stand anywhere quiet.
gym: Find a quiet corner or sit on a bench.

home: Use a sturdy chair without wheels.
gym: Sit on a flat bench or the end of a machine seat that does not move.

home: Use a smooth wall; place a mat under your feet so they do not slide.
gym: Use a wall or the back of a fixed machine; keep knees above ankles.

home: Stand next to a wall, counter or chair back.
gym: Hold a rack or machine frame lightly for safety.

home: At home, anchor a resistance band high on a closed door and pull down while kneeling.
gym: Adjust the thigh pad so you cannot lift off the seat.
Use a grip just wider than shoulders; thumbs around the bar.
Pull to the top of your chest, never behind the neck.
Pick a weight you can pull without swinging your body.

home: At home, loop a resistance band around a sturdy post or your feet and row while sitting tall.
gym: Use the V-handle with palms facing each other.
Keep your chest up; do not lean back more than a little.
Pull elbows close to your sides toward your hips.

home: At home, anchor a resistance band high on a door and push down the same way.
gym: Pin your elbows to your sides; only the forearms move.
With a rope, spread the ends apart at the bottom.
Choose a weight you can control without leaning over it.
Set the seat so your elbows are level with your shoulders.
Keep shoulders down and back against the pad.
Stop opening when you feel a gentle stretch, not pain in the shoulder.

home: At home, do push-ups or knee push-ups for the same muscles.
gym: Set the seat so handles are at mid-chest, not at the neck.
Grip with wrists straight and elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Breathe out as you press, in as you return.

home: At home, do bodyweight squats or wall sits instead.
gym: Feet flat, hip-width, in the middle of the platform.
Lower only as far as your lower back stays on the pad.
Lock the safety handles before getting out.

home: At home, do slow seated knee extensions on a chair or bodyweight squats.
gym: Line up your knee with the red pivot dot on the machine.
Hold the side handles to keep your hips on the seat.
Use a light weight and move slowly; stop if the knee hurts.

home: At home, do glute bridges or a hip hinge to train the back of the legs.
gym: Line up your knees with the pivot point of the machine.
Lower the thigh pad until it holds your legs firmly.
Hold the handles and move slowly in both directions.
Set safety arms just below chest height or ask for a spotter.
Squeeze shoulder blades together and keep feet flat.
Wrists straight over elbows; start with the empty bar.
Learn the hip hinge first; start with a light bar or plates on blocks.
Keep the bar touching your legs the whole time.
Never round your back to reach the bar.

home: At home, use dumbbells or practise the bodyweight hip hinge.
gym: Start from standing (take the bar from a rack).
Keep the bar close to your legs.
Go down only as far as your back stays flat.

home: At home, use dumbbells (dumbbell bent-over row).
gym: Grip just wider than shoulders, palms facing you.
Keep your torso still; only the arms move.
Use a light weight first to learn the position.

home: At home, use a resistance band anchored behind you for a standing fly.
gym: Stand in the middle of the station with a split stance.
Keep the elbow bend the same throughout.
Use a light weight; the movement should feel smooth.

home: Use a mat; keep your chin slightly tucked and do not pull on your neck.
gym: Use a mat; for more challenge hold a light plate on your chest.

home: Use a mat; lift only a small height without pain.
gym: Use a mat, or use the back extension bench with a small range.

home: Use dumbbells or filled water bottles; stand against a wall to stop swinging.
gym: Pick dumbbells you can lift without leaning back; a rope on a low cable also works.

home: Use a sturdy chair against a wall so it cannot slide; keep knees bent for an easier version.
gym: Use a flat bench; straighten your legs only when the bent-knee version is easy.

home: At home, squeeze a pillow or ball between your knees while lying on your back.
gym: Start with a small range; widen it only if your hips feel comfortable.
Keep your back against the pad the whole time.

home: At home, use a dumbbell shoulder press with light weights.
gym: Keep your feet flat and your ribs down so your back stays on the pad.
Stop just before your elbows lock.

home: At home, do band rows instead.
gym: Start with plenty of assistance and reduce it over the weeks.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears as you pull.

home: At home, do glute bridges or slider leg curls on a smooth floor.
gym: Keep your hips down on the bench.
Use a weight you can lower slowly.

home: At home, do bodyweight squats.
gym: Always set the safety stops first.
Go only as low as you can keep your back straight.

home: At home, do wall sits or bodyweight squats.
gym: Start light; this machine is harder than the leg press.
Keep your knees in line with your toes.

home: At home, do standing calf raises on a step.
gym: Move slowly and pause at the top.
Push through the big toe side of your foot.

home: At home, do dumbbell or band curls.
gym: Stand tall and keep your elbows still.
Use a weight you can control on the way down.

home: At home, do incline push-ups with hands on a sturdy table.
gym: A low incline (about 30 degrees) is enough.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees from your body.

home: At home, use a water bottle or a band.
gym: Keep your upper arm still and close to your body.
Choose a light weight; form matters more.

home: At home, use a water bottle or a light dumbbell.
gym: Sitting on a bench with back support makes it easier to keep good form.
Keep your ribs down so your back does not arch.

home: At home, do glute bridges on the floor.
gym: Use a bar pad for comfort.
Keep your chin tucked and ribs down at the top.

home: At home, do band rows or table rows if you have no bar.
gym: Use the assisted machine first if you cannot do 5 good reps.
Keep your body still; no swinging.

home: At home, use water bottles or a band.
gym: Very light weights are enough for this small muscle.
Lead with your elbows, not your hands.

home: At home, do dumbbell or band curls.
gym: An EZ bar is easier on the wrists.
Keep your body still; no swinging.
